note: Hand-checked. Every number is what the named source reported; where sources differ the range or the cut-off date is given. 'river' events get a downstream trace from the origin; 'site' events are point outbreaks (water system, well, lake intake).

events.name: Cholera, Haiti
events.agent: Vibrio cholerae O1, El Tor, Ogawa
events.count_note: Suspected cases and deaths, October 2010 - February 2019 (WHO). Haiti's ministry: 819,786 cases, 9,789 deaths to December 2018.
events.water: The first hospitalised patients lived in Meille, beside a UN peacekeeping camp built above a stream that flows into the Artibonite River; sewage from the camp reached the stream. Cases then exploded downstream in the Artibonite delta and coastal plain, among people who drank river water.
sources: Piarroux et al. 2011, Emerging Infectious Diseases 17(7)

events.name: Cholera, Zimbabwe

origin.place: Chitungwiza (St Mary's and Zengeza wards), near Harare

events.count_note: Reported to the end of July 2009 (Mukandavire et al., PNAS 2011). Other tallies give up to 4,369 deaths.
events.water: First cases reported on 20 August 2008. Broken water supply and overflowing sewers in a crowded town with chronic water shortages; it spread to all provinces.

events.name: Cholera, Yemen
events.count_note: Suspected cases and deaths to March 2021 (WHO EMRO); one of the largest cholera outbreaks ever recorded. 2021-2022 added fewer than 40,000 suspected cases.
events.water: War-damaged water and sewage networks; the outbreak peaked in 2017.

events.name: Cholera, Malawi
events.count_note: Cumulative to 7 April 2024 (WHO); Malawi's worst cholera outbreak in decades. Case fatality 3.0 %.
events.water: First case registered in Machinga District on 2 March 2022; by mid-2023 all 29 districts had reported cases.

events.name: Cholera returns to the Americas, Peru
events.agent: Vibrio cholerae O1, El Tor, Inaba
events.count_note: All of the Americas to 28 August 1991 (PAHO); most cases were in Peru.
events.water: The first cholera epidemic in South America in the 20th century. It ran along about 2,000 km of the populated coast within two weeks, through untreated drinking water and food.

events.name: Cryptosporidium, Milwaukee

origin.place: Howard Avenue water treatment plant (Lake Michigan intake)

events.count_note: About 403,000 people fell ill (MacKenzie et al., NEJM 1994). Reported deaths range from 69 to over 100 immunocompromised people, depending on the study.
events.water: The largest documented waterborne outbreak in US history. Oocysts passed the plant's filters; the most likely source was sewage reaching its Lake Michigan intake, but the cause was never officially confirmed.

events.name: E. coli O157:H7, Walkerton
events.agent: E. coli O157:H7 and Campylobacter jejuni
events.water: Heavy rain on 8-12 May 2000 washed cattle manure from a nearby farm into a shallow town well; continuous chlorine and turbidity monitoring would have prevented it (O'Connor inquiry).
sources: Report of the Walkerton Inquiry, Part 1 summary

events.name: Cyanide spill, Baia Mare

origin.place: Aurul tailings dam, Baia Mare, Romania

events.count_note: 50-100 t of cyanide released; about 1,240 t of fish killed in Hungary.
events.water: Through the Lapus, Somes and Tisza into the Danube; still measurable in the Danube delta about four weeks later.
sources: UNEP/OCHA assessment mission, Cyanide spill at Baia Mare, 2000
ICPDR Danube Watch, the 2000 cyanide incident

events.name: Benzene spill, Songhua River

origin.place: Jilin Petrochemical plant, Jilin City, China

events.count_note: An explosion released about 100 t of benzene compounds. Harbin shut off its water supply from 23 November.
events.water: The slick moved down the Songhua under forming ice, past Harbin, into the Amur (Heilongjiang) and on to Khabarovsk in Russia.

events.name: Tailings dam collapse, Rio Doce
events.count_note: 19 people died. The mud travelled 620-670 km to the Atlantic.
events.water: Through the Gualaxo do Norte and Carmo into the Rio Doce; reached the Atlantic at Regência about 17 days later.
sources: Marta-Almeida et al. 2016, Fundão Dam collapse: oceanic dispersion of River Doce

events.name: Sandoz chemical fire, Rhine
events.agent: Pesticides and mercury compounds in fire-fighting water
events.count_note: Tonnes of agrochemicals washed into the Rhine with fire-fighting water from about 01:30 on 1 November 1986; mass eel kill downstream.
events.water: The red pollution wave moved down the Rhine through Germany and the Netherlands to the North Sea. It led to the Rhine Action Programme of 1987.
sources: Giger 2009, The Rhine red, the fish dead - the 1986 Schweizerhalle disaster

references.name: Rhine water transit
references.note: Water takes approximately nine days from Rheinfelden to the catchment outlet at Lobith (water itself, not the faster flood wave).
source: GIS-based water balance model for the Rhine drainage basin (ResearchGate)
